cues: The major shipping agent-memory systems we checked ask a model whether their own memory is true. Mem0, Zep, AWS AgentCore.
MemoryStand asks CloudWatch instead, and refuses the promotion when CloudWatch disagrees. Here it is doing that, live.
A runbook fact goes in first, live: checkout-api's breaker trips at 800 milliseconds. Nothing on file contradicts it, so it's accepted.
A Slack claim arrives next, saying 300 milliseconds, with no runbook behind it. Slack doesn't outrank a runbook, so that claim is held for review, not thrown away.
The on-call lead corrects it, live: 500 milliseconds, the real number. A human outranks a runbook, so this is accepted, and recorded as corrected by a higher-authority source.
The 800-millisecond fact stays on record, not deleted — the Slack guess is still just held, nobody confirmed it.

scenes.evidenceClass: LIVE AWS · OUTCOME PATH · STUB EMBEDDINGS
cues: An incident hits: payments-gateway latency is spiking. Recall surfaces the corrected five-hundred-millisecond fact, and the agent reasons over it.
This is a real model call. The rationale cites the memory it used, by id, and proposes one action from a closed allow-list -- it cannot invent an action that is not on the list.
One honest disclosure: this AWS account has zero Bedrock quota, so embeddings are still a lexical stub, not semantic. Recall matches wording, not meaning.
The incident resolves in PagerDuty. That's a real external signal, so the memory moves up -- but only to attested, because nothing here can re-check PagerDuty.
Now a metric claim: latency fell. MemoryStand re-queries CloudWatch, CloudWatch agrees, and only now does the memory reach verified. Model calls to decide that: zero.
And when the claim is wrong, watch. Claimed ten milliseconds; CloudWatch says eleven thousand four hundred and fifty-two. Refused. A memory gains nothing from a claim its own metric contradicts.
This part isn't new — Zep and others already ship bitemporal replay.

What this proves is a real pinned read: AS OF SYSTEM TIME re-runs the exact query at the instant the decision was made, against the live database, not a reconstruction. Then it's diffed against what's true right now.

Separately, on a real three-node cluster, we kill a node mid-recall. Twelve reads, zero failures, all 101 memories still there. Three containers on one machine — this proves the replication mechanism, not a datacenter failing.
At 250,000 memories on that cluster, indexed recall held at 6.87 milliseconds against 526 unindexed: 76.5 times faster.
None of this is a new idea. Doyle's truth maintenance systems retracted beliefs when their justification failed, in 1979. Bitemporal replay ships in Zep today.

What is measured is the difference. Against six hundred poisoned claims plus honest controls: trusting the caller admits every attack. An LLM judge blocks every attack -- and every honest claim too, so it is useless. Only the outcome gate tells them apart.
Hackathon build: candidate only, no general-intelligence claim, code's public.
